full_judgment:
4. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, learned Advocate for the petitioners, raised only one point for our consideration which, however, was not argued in the High Court Division. The point is that inasmuch as the alleged offences are said to have been committed by private persons and not by public servants, no officer of the Bureau of Anti-Corruption is authorised to make any investigation against the petitioners of the alleged offences. In support of his submission Mr. Hossain has referred to the case of Abul Basher vs. State 47 DLR 521 decided by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in which an observation has been made that: "It also shows that the offences under the schedule must be relatable to public servant." 

 "3 CONSTITUTION AND POWERS OF THE BUREAU - (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the police Act, 1861 (v of 1861), the Government may constitute a Bureau to be called the Bureau of Anti-Corruption for enquiry into and investigation in Bangladesh of the offences specified in the schedule and offences notified by the Government. 

 "(c) offences punishable under section 120B, 161 to 169, 201, 217, 218 379 to 382, 403 to 409, 411, 414, 417 to 420, 465 to 468, 474, 477A and 511 of the penal code (Act X1L of 1860)".
